primitives.name: Constant Velocity Kalman Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: One way to create coherent trajectories is by applying a constant velocity Kalman *Equal contribution Filter (KF) [2].
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear motion with constant velocity and Gaussian noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when non-linear dynamics dominate or noise covariance is misspecified.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Models posterior predictive distributions for latent states. GSE: Encodes state transitions via Markov kernels.
layer2.telemetry: Track continuity metrics and outlier rejection rates.

primitives.name: Tracking-by-Detection Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: A common approach is Tracking-by-detection [1–3], a two-step approach that first detects the objects in each frame of the video, and associates these detections over time to form trajectories (tracks).
primitives.assumptions: Relies on accurate per-frame object detection and reliable association metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under severe occlusions, scale variations, and low detection recall.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Treats detection scores as likelihood ratios for Bayesian updating. GSE: Uses association metrics to compute transition probabilities between states.
layer2.telemetry: Association accuracy and detection confidence thresholds.

primitives.name: DeepOC-SORT Re-Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Ball tracking is formulated as single object detection, and a fine-tuned YOLOv8l detector with proprietary filtering improves the detection precision.
primitives.assumptions: Utilizes learned appearance features to bridge gaps between disjoint tracks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when appearance changes drastically or training data mismatch occurs.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Implements conformal prediction sets based on learned embeddings. GSE: Integrates re-identification into state-transition models for persistent entity tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Re-identification accuracy and track fragmentation rate.

primitives.name: Ball Detection as Single Object Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Ball tracking is formulated as single object detection, and a fine-tuned YOLOv8l detector with proprietary filtering improves the detection precision.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes distinct visual characteristics of the ball compared to other scene elements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Struggles in dense scenes with similar colored objects or extreme lighting changes.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Treats ball presence as a binary hypothesis test with sequential probability ratio test. GSE: Models ball state transitions as a specialized sub-system within the full tracking graph.
layer2.telemetry: Detection precision and false alarm rate for the ball.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is fusing noisy spatial measurements across frames while managing computational constraints for live streaming. The Kalman Filter excels at smoothing linear dynamics but fails under abrupt changes. Tracking-by-Detection decouples perception from association, enabling modular updates but suffers from ID switches. DeepOC-SORT addresses ID persistence through appearance learning, yet requires substantial training data. Ball detection simplifies to a classification problem, but domain-specific filtering is crucial. These primitives interoperate via telemetry feedback: detection confidence informs Kalman priors, re-identification scores guide track mergers, and ball presence triggers specialized state updates. Failure modes include drift due to model bias, fragmentation from poor associations, and catastrophic forgetting in concept-evolving domains.
